details.note: Filters common web attacks and rate-limits each address before traffic reaches the load balancer.
Ends TLS and spreads requests across the web servers. Its health checks take a failing server out of rotation.
Renders pages and serves static files. Keep web servers stateless so you can add one behind the load balancer at any time.
Internal only: nothing outside the web tier can reach it.
Runs the business logic: recipes, ratings, search. Sessions live in the cache, not in memory.
The only place recipes, members and ratings are written.
Takes heavy search and reporting reads off the primary. It can lag by a second or two.
Sessions and hot recipe pages, so any app server can answer any request.
Recipe photos as objects; the database stores only their keys.
Metrics and logs from every tier. Alert on error rate and slow pages, not on CPU alone.

name: Three-tier web app
note: Swap the recipe site for your own app but keep the three tiers: web servers handle requests, app servers run the logic, and only the data tier holds state. Each tier talks only to the next one in, so write the protocol on every arrow and keep each tier in its own subnet.
title: Recipe sharing site
